title: What Happens When an Airway Reopens? — Evidence Cut
format: 1920? no: 1280x720, 24fps, real published figure + labeled original schematics and reported in-vitro values
paper: Dexamethasone and transdehydroandrosterone significantly reduce pulmonary epithelial cell injuries associated with mechanical ventilation
note: These are published mean percentage cell-death results for cell populations under a single-bubble in-vitro model, not clinical treatment effects or independent reproduction. Published article reports variability ±3.94, ±3.43, ±2.9 and ±12 respectively. The bar visualization shows means only and does not infer error-bar type or digitize new data.

scenes.title: Reopening is not always gentle
scenes.narration: A narrowed, fluid-filled airway can reopen as air moves through it. Yet the advancing air–liquid boundary may impose forces on the very epithelial cells it passes.

scenes.title: A boundary that moves
scenes.narration: The experiment is not a miniature human lung. It is a controlled way to study what happens when one air bubble travels across a cell layer in a liquid-lined channel.

scenes.title: Inside the flow chamber
scenes.narration: In our 2021 study, rat L2 alveolar epithelial cells were grown in a parallel-plate flow chamber. A single advancing bubble simulated the mechanical event of airway reopening.

scenes.title: The comparison
scenes.narration: We compared cells kept under static conditions with cells exposed to bubble flow. We also tested cells pretreated with dexamethasone or transdehydroandrosterone before the bubble passed.

scenes.title: How cell injury was read
scenes.narration: Fluorescence staining distinguished live from dead cells. Cytoskeletal staining and atomic force microscopy added information about the cells' shape, actin structure, and mechanical response.

scenes.title: The unprotected group
scenes.narration: Following bubble propagation, the untreated group showed 54.7 percent cell death in this model. The reported comparison is about cultured cells, not a patient survival rate.

scenes.title: Dexamethasone pretreatment
scenes.narration: With dexamethasone pretreatment, reported cell death after bubble exposure was 15.1 percent. That is a substantial reduction compared with the bubble-only control under these specific conditions.

scenes.title: Transdehydroandrosterone
scenes.narration: Cells pretreated with transdehydroandrosterone showed 16.1 percent cell death after exposure. Both treatments were associated with protection in the laboratory setup; neither figure describes clinical efficacy.

scenes.title: Another mechanical comparison
scenes.narration: The study also included latrunculin A, an experimental cytoskeletal agent. Its bubble-exposed group showed 20.9 percent cell death, helping relate susceptibility to cell mechanics.

scenes.title: The cytoskeleton matters
scenes.kind: MECHANISTIC INTERPRETATION / NOT PROOF OF A SINGLE PATHWAY
scenes.narration: Actin organization and mechanical properties were examined alongside viability. The study supports investigating cell mechanics as part of protection, while leaving complex molecular causality open.

scenes.title: What the experiment can say
scenes.narration: These are results from a single-bubble, cultured-cell model. They justify further questions about injury prevention. They do not show that pretreatment prevents injury in mechanically ventilated patients.
